text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-The General Labour Confederation (CGTL) demands a 20 percent wage increase for Lebanese workers backdated to 1/1/1997.
-Lebanon's 1996 debt reached $10.348 billion and the annual budget deficit was 3,692 billion Lebanese pounds.
-Prime Minister Hariri tells Minister of Industry Salem the decision to cut by 10 percent taxes on all imported clothes was frozen.
-Pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia released Lebanese doctor Nakd who was arrested and held at Khiam prison for 82 days.
-A judicial committee affirmed a magistrate's order to release on bail three Iraqi diplomats suspected of involvement in the 1994 murder of Iraqi dissident Taleb as-Suheil in Beirut.
-About 1.7 million passengers used Beirut International Airport in 1996.
-General Labour Confederation demands forming a full mandate court to investigate corruption accusations mentioned recently by top officials.
-The Bank of Lebanon issued certificates of deposit dated January 24 to commercial banks worth 27 billion Lebanese pounds.
-Head of the rightwing Christian National Liberal Party Chamoun said:"I do not recognize the legality of this rule in Lebanon".
-Israeli forces arrested three women in the south Lebanon occupation zone.
